## Get reactome gene sets

```{r,reactome}

gmt_import <- function(gmtfile) {
    genesetLines <- strsplit(readLines(gmtfile), "\t")
    genesets <- lapply(genesetLines, utils::tail, -2)
    names(genesets) <- unlist(lapply(genesetLines, head, 1))
    attributes(genesets)$originfile <- gmtfile
    genesets <- genesets[lapply(genesets,length)>0]
    if( any(duplicated(names(genesets))) ) {
        warning("Duplicated gene sets names detected")
    }
    genesets
}

gs <- gmt_import("ReactomePathways_2026-10-23.gmt")

names(gs) <- sapply(1:length(gs), function(i) {
  set.seed(i*100)
  paste(sample(x=letters, size=20, replace=TRUE), collapse="",sep="")
} )


```

## Downsample

Simulate some differential gene expression data

Effect size distributions

low=seq(0.4,0.8,0.1)

medium=seq(0.5,1.2,0.1)

high=seq(0.8,1.6,0.1)

```{r,downsample_simulation_function}

FC=c("low","medium","high")

gsets=gs

simcounts <- function(counts, N_REPS=5, SUM_COUNT=20e6, VARIANCE=0.2, FRAC_DE_PW=0.1, effect="medium", gsets, seed=1) {

  # Use edgeR::thincounts to create pseudoreplicate datasets
  df  = NULL
  for (k in paste0("data",1:(N_REPS*2)))  {
    set.seed(seed*100)
    b <- thinCounts(a,target.size=SUM_COUNT)
    colnames(b) <- k
    df <- cbind(df,b)
  }

  ## Put some variance into the samples!
  if (VARIANCE > 0) {
    #create some random values centred around 1 with some% error
    rand <- matrix(log2(rnorm(nrow(a)*N_REPS*2 , 2, VARIANCE)),ncol=N_REPS*2)
    #incorporate the noise
    df <- round(df*rand)
    #set any negative counts to zero
    df <- apply(df, 2, function(x) { ifelse(x < 0, 0, x) })
  }

  # Select gene sets with more than 10 members present in the matrix
  gsets_sub <- which(unlist( lapply(gsets,function(x) {
    length(which(rownames(a) %in% as.character(unlist(x)))) >10
  }  ) ) )
  gsets <- gsets[which(names(gsets) %in% names(gsets_sub))]

  NDIF=round(length(gsets)*FRAC_DE)
  if ( NDIF%%2==1 ) { print("odd") ; NDIF=NDIF-1 }

  if ( effect == "low" ) {
    FC_VALS <- seq(0.4,0.8,0.1)
  }
  if ( effect == "medium" ) {
    FC_VALS <- seq(0.5,1.2,0.1)
  }
  if ( effect == "high" ) {
    FC_VALS <- seq(0.8,1.6,0.1)
  }

  # generate target numbers for each pathway
  set.seed(seed*1000)
  PWFC <- sample(x=FC_VALS,size=NDIF,replace=TRUE)

  # Flip half the signs
  PWFC <- PWFC * ( ( ( 1:length(PWFC) %% 2 ) *2 ) -1 )

  # Select the DE pathways and genes
  set.seed(seed*10000)
  DEPW_LIST <- sample(gsets , NDIF)
  # dataframe of pathway name and LOGFC
  DEPW_DF <- data.frame(names(DEPW_LIST),PWFC)
  DEGENES <- unique(unlist(DEPW_LIST))

  # for each DEGENE, get the fold change of it
  # which will be a product of all the
  DELFC <- sapply(DEGENES, function(g) {
    matches <- names(which(sapply(DEPW_LIST, function(mygs) {
      length(which( mygs == g ))
    } ) == 1))
    LFC <- prod( DEPW_DF[match(matches, DEPW_DF[,1]),2] )
    return(LFC)
  } )
  names(DELFC) <- DEGENES

  # Now because the final FC of each gene is a product
  # we can find the mean of all the gene in the set
  # correlation of 0.7 between planned and final pathway level FCs
  DEPW_DF$final_LFC <- sapply(DEPW_DF$names.DEPW_LIST., function(mygs) {
    setgenes <- DEPW_LIST[[which(names(DEPW_LIST) == mygs)]]
    final_LFC <- mean(DELFC[which(names(DELFC) %in% setgenes)])
    return(final_LFC)
  } )

  ## Now simply incorporate these fold changes
  # get the steady genes with no change
  NCnames <- rownames(df[which(! rownames(df) %in% names(DELFC) ),])
  NCvec <- rep(x=1,times=length(NCnames))
  names(NCvec) <- NCnames
  # combine with the DE fold changes converted from log to linear scale
  FCvec <- c(2^DELFC,NCvec)
  FCvec <- FCvec[match(rownames(df),names(FCvec))]
  # apply fold changes to case group
  CASE <- df[,(N_REPS+1):ncol(df)]
  CASE <- round(apply(CASE,2, function(x) { x * FCvec } ))
  # no changes to ctrl group
  CTRL <- df[,1:N_REPS]
  # output the combined
  df2 <- as.data.frame(cbind(CTRL,CASE))
  out <- list("a"=df2,"fcdf"=DEPW_DF)
  return(out)
}

testdata <- simcounts(counts=a, N_REPS=5, SUM_COUNT=20e6,
  VARIANCE=0.3, FRAC_DE_PW=0.1, effect="medium", gsets=gs, seed=100)

str(testdata)

```

## Function for running FGSEA

Run fgsea and see if the NES prioritisation works.

Run a basic test to show GT pathways are actually altered with FDR selection.

Yes it confirms the ability of FGSEA to identify these pathways but OMG there are
a lot of false positives.

```{r,benchmark_fgsea}

# the data object is a list that contains 1 count matrix and 1 DF of PW fold changes
run_fgsea <- function(data,  gsets, seed=1) {
  mx <- data[[1]]
  ss <- data.frame(colnames(mx))
  ss$group <- c( rep(x="ctrl",times=nrow(ss)/2)  , rep(x="trt",times=nrow(ss)/2) )
  rownames(ss) <- ss[,1]
  design <- model.matrix(~ group, data = ss)
  y <- DGEList(counts = mx)
  y <- normLibSizes(y)
  v <- voom(y, design)
  fit <- lmFit(v, design)
  fit2 <- eBayes(fit)
  results <- topTable(fit2, coef = "grouptrt", number = Inf, adjust.method = "fdr")
  stats <- results$t
  names(stats) <- rownames(results)
  set.seed(seed*100)
  fres <- fgsea(pathways=gsets, stats=stats, minSize=5 )
  fres <- as.data.frame(fres)
  fres <- fres[order(fres$pval),]
  fcdf <- data[[2]]
  out <- list("a"=mx, "fcdf"=fcdf, "fres"=fres)
}

test_fgsea <- run_fgsea(data=testdata, gsets=gs, seed=1)
head(test_fgsea[[3]])

test_fgsea_up <- subset(test_fgsea[[3]], padj < 0.05 & ES > 0 )$pathway
test_fgsea_dn <- subset(test_fgsea[[3]], padj < 0.05 & ES < 0 )$pathway

gt_up <- subset(test_fgsea[[2]],final_LFC>0)[,1]
gt_dn <- subset(test_fgsea[[2]],final_LFC<0)[,1]

v1 <- list("FCS up"=test_fgsea_up, "FCS dn"=test_fgsea_dn, "GT up"=gt_up, "GT_dn"=gt_dn)

plot(euler(v1),quantities = TRUE)

```

Now do the same for ORA.

We can see that ORA yields more false positives from this single test.
I will need to run a lot more simulations to understand this in more
detail.

```{r,benchmark_ora}

run_fora <- function(data,  gsets) {
  mx <- data[[1]]
  ss <- data.frame(colnames(mx))
  ss$group <- c( rep(x="ctrl",times=nrow(ss)/2)  , rep(x="trt",times=nrow(ss)/2) )
  rownames(ss) <- ss[,1]
  design <- model.matrix(~ group, data = ss)
  y <- DGEList(counts = mx)
  y <- normLibSizes(y)
  v <- voom(y, design)
  fit <- lmFit(v, design)
  fit2 <- eBayes(fit)
  results <- topTable(fit2, coef = "grouptrt", number = Inf, adjust.method = "fdr")
  # select genes for ORA
  up <- unique(rownames(head(subset(results, logFC>0),1000)))
  dn <- unique(rownames(head(subset(results, logFC<0),1000)))
  bg <- unique(rownames(results))
  ores_up <- fora(pathways=gs,genes=up,universe=bg,minSize=5)
  ores_dn <- fora(pathways=gs,genes=dn,universe=bg,minSize=5)
  # flip enrichment sign for down genes
  ores_dn$foldEnrichment <- ores_dn$foldEnrichment * -1
  # combine separate tests for up and down into single output
  o_comb <- lapply(ores_up$pathway, function(x) {
    upES <- subset(ores_up,pathway==x)[,"foldEnrichment"]
    dnES <-  subset(ores_dn,pathway==x)[,"foldEnrichment"]
    if ( abs(upES) >= abs(dnES) ) {
      subset(ores_up,pathway==x)
    } else {
      subset(ores_dn,pathway==x)
    }
  } )
  ores <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind,o_comb))
  fcdf <- data[[2]]
  out <- list("a"=mx, "fcdf"=fcdf, "ores"=ores)
  return(out)
}

test_fora <- run_fora(data=testdata,  gsets=gs)

test_fora_up <- subset(test_fora[[3]], padj < 0.05 & foldEnrichment > 0 )$pathway
test_fora_dn <- subset(test_fora[[3]], padj < 0.05 & foldEnrichment < 0 )$pathway

gt_up <- subset(test_fora[[2]],final_LFC>0)[,1]
gt_dn <- subset(test_fora[[2]],final_LFC<0)[,1]

v1 <- list("ORA up"=test_fora_up, "ORA dn"=test_fora_dn, "GT up"=gt_up, "GT_dn"=gt_dn)

plot(euler(v1),quantities = TRUE)

```
